metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Block Bindings APIs

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers a server-side block binding source named 'wpbp/source' that can replace a bound paragraph's content with the binding's 'text' argument.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_gb_block_bindings_001()` registers the `wpbp/source` binding source with WordPress and returns whether the source is registered. Runtime validation renders a paragraph whose `content` attribute is bound to the source and confirms WordPress replaces the fallback text with the binding argument.

Register the source name 'wpbp/source'
Return whether WordPress registered the source

tests.prompt: Implement a function that makes WordPress treat the 'title' attribute of the custom block type 'wpbp/card' as bindable without changing bindable attributes for unrelated block types.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_gb_block_bindings_002()` hooks the Block Bindings supported-attributes API for `wpbp/card`, preserves existing attribute lists, and adds `title` only for that block type. Runtime validation registers a dynamic `wpbp/card` fixture, binds its `title` attribute to a source, and confirms WordPress passes the bound title into the block render callback.
requirements: Use the supported block attributes filter
Target only the 'wpbp/card' block type
Preserve existing supported attributes

assertions.code:
if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_gb_block_bindings_002' ) ) { return false; } register_block_type( 'wpbp/card', array( 'attributes' => array( 'title' => array( 'type' => 'string', 'default' => 'Fallback Card' ) ), 'render_callback' => static fn( array $attrs ): string => '
' . esc_html( $attrs['title'] ?? '' ) . '
' ) ); register_block_bindings_source( 'wpbp/card-title-source', array( 'label' => 'Card Title Source', 'get_value_callback' => static fn(): string => 'Bound Card' ) ); wpbp_gb_block_bindings_002(); $card_attrs = get_block_bindings_supported_attributes( 'wpbp/card' ); $paragraph_attrs = get_block_bindings_supported_attributes( 'core/paragraph' ); $content = ''; $out = trim( do_blocks( $content ) ); return in_array( 'title', $card_attrs, true ) && ! in_array( 'title', $paragraph_attrs, true ) && '

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_gb_block_bindings_002(): void { add_filter( 'block_bindings_supported_attributes', static function ( array $supported_attributes, string $block_type ): array { if ( 'wpbp/card' !== $block_type ) { return $supported_attributes; } if ( ! in_array( 'title', $supported_attributes, true ) ) { $supported_attributes[] = 'title'; } return $supported_attributes; }, 10, 2 ); }

tests.prompt: The 'wpbp_book' custom post type keeps each book's shelf code in the 'wpbp_shelf_code' post meta field. Editors should not have to retype it: a list item in the book's content should take its text from that field through WordPress's built-in post meta binding source. Implement the rendering of such a list for a given book - a list block holding a single bound list item whose saved placeholder text is 'Unknown' - and make sure the binding source is actually allowed to read that meta field.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: the core/post-meta source refuses any key that is protected or not registered with show_in_rest for the post's subtype, so the meta must be registered with register_meta() using object_subtype 'wpbp_book', single true and show_in_rest true. The list item carries metadata.bindings.content pointing at core/post-meta with args.key, which 7.1 supports for core/list-item, and the block instance must be given both postId and postType context because the source declares both. Rendering two books yields their two different codes and no placeholder; rendering without post context leaves the placeholder in place.
requirements: Take the book's post ID and return the rendered markup as a string.
Register the shelf code meta field so the built-in post meta binding source is permitted to read it.
Bind the list item's own text rather than rewriting the list markup afterwards.
Give the rendered block the post context the binding source needs.
Keep 'Unknown' as the placeholder text in the markup you build.

required_patterns.description: Uses the built-in post meta binding source
Binds the shelf code meta key
Exposes the meta field to the binding source

tests.prompt: A synced pattern can expose named blocks whose text an individual placement of that pattern may override, while the pattern itself stays shared. Given the post ID of such a synced pattern and a map of overridable block names to replacement text, render that pattern with the replacements applied to just those blocks. Blocks the map does not mention, and names that do not appear in the pattern, must render the pattern's own content.
tests.expected_behavior: Reviewer contract: the overrides travel as the core/block instance's 'content' attribute, which the block provides to its inner blocks as the 'pattern/overrides' context. The core/pattern-overrides source looks the value up at context['pattern/overrides'][ metadata.name ][ attribute ], so the map value must be an array keyed by attribute name - array( 'content' => $text ) - not a bare string. The legacy 'overrides' attribute name no longer works because core/block declares a default for 'content', so the back-compat branch never runs. Unmatched names simply resolve to null and the saved text stands.
requirements: Take the synced pattern's post ID and the overrides map, and return the rendered HTML.
Apply the overrides through the pattern instance itself, not by editing the stored pattern or rewriting the rendered HTML.
Leave blocks the map does not name untouched.

required_patterns.description: Points the instance at the pattern post

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_gb_block_bindings_006( int $pattern_id, array $overrides ): string { $content = array(); foreach ( $overrides as $name => $text ) { $content[ $name ] = array( 'content' => $text ); } return render_block( array( 'blockName' => 'core/block', 'attrs' => array( 'ref' => $pattern_id, 'content' => $content ), 'innerBlocks' => array(), 'innerHTML' => '', 'innerContent' => array() ) ); }
